text:
maggie: Quick follow-up to the prefetch RFC — I've sketched a small API for a 'soft-prefetch operator' that the compact planner can call before evicting slabs. Wanted to sync on boundaries and fallback semantics.
andre: +1 for syncing. can you paste the sketch?
olena: curious how this differs from existing prefetch hints we already push from the scheduler.
maggie: sure — rough idea: planner calls operator with `range_id`, `priority`, and `deadline_ms`. operator returns an admission token or a reason code. Example: 
```
PrefetchRequest { range_id: u64, priority: u8, deadline_ms: u32 }
PrefetchResponse { status: enum {Admitted, Throttled, NotSupported, Error}, token: Option<u64> }
```
andre: nice. so token semantics: if Admitted you get guaranteed prefetch done before deadline? or best-effort?
maggie: design choice. leaning toward "best-effort with ack" — no strict guarantees. token acts as a leash to optionally extend residency while prefetch completes. planner can decide to delay eviction until token is released or until deadline.
ryan: OK but how do we avoid head-of-line blocking on large ranges? we need a prefetch budget and backpressure.
olena: budget should live with the operator — operator enforces concurrency, throttles by tenant, and returns Throttled when over budget. planner should fall back immediately to local compact strategies when Throttled/NotSupported.
andre: fallback semantics need to be explicit. if prefetch fails, planner should try: 1) compact in-place 2) incremental migrate to host staging 3) drop to lower-quality quantized backing. order configurable per tenant.
maggie: agree — we should encode a small `FallbackPolicy` blob with the request, e.g. `FALLBACK=[compact, host_migrate, quantize]`. operator ignores it but planner uses it if response != Admitted.
ryan: telemetry: events we need: request_sent, admitted, token_released, throttled_reason, prefetch_latency, bytes_moved. Also gauge for active_prefetch_tokens per tenant.
olena: add metric for prefetch_success_rate and a histogram for deadline_miss. we'll need these for rollout SLOs.
and re: compatibility: older operators may not understand token semantics. NotSupported status covers that. planner should detect and enable conservative mode (no delays) per operator capability.
maggie: rollout plan: feature-flagged in runtime, start with small fraction of tenants, observe prefetch_success_rate and latency, then widen. we'll add per-tenant opt-outs.
ryan: test plan: unit tests for request/response plumbing, integration test where operator returns Throttled, and a chaos test that kills operator mid-prefetch to validate planner falls back cleanly.
olena: code-wise, where do we put the operator hook? likely in the residency manager API as `request_soft_prefetch(req) -> resp`. keep it async.
and re: propose signature: `async fn request_soft_prefetch(req: PrefetchRequest) -> PrefetchResponse` plus `async fn release_prefetch(token: u64)`. document token lifespan and id recycling.
maggie: sounds good. I'll draft a short RFC addendum with example flows and the metrics table. any objections to adding the token release call (explicit) vs implicit TTL?
ryan: explicit release is better for sanity and easier telemetry. implicit TTL as safety net if client forgets.
olena: +1. also flag: make sure this doesn't give planners a way to starve other tenants — quota enforcement must be operator-side.
andre: agreed. I'll open a PR with the API types and a mocked operator for tests.
maggie: thanks all — I'll drop the RFC addendum in the docs folder and ping infra for canary rollout. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: deploy-check: canary flag created for soft-prefetch (ff/soft_prefetch_opt) — ready for infra sandbox testing.
